resolutions.original_unknown: Exact decay schedule for the gradual-filtering ratios r_1 > r_2 > ... > r is not specified (Section 4.3 gives only the qualitative rule).
resolutions.resolution: The released reference implementation does NOT use a per-layer decaying schedule r_1 > r_2 > ... > r. Instead it uses a single 'check layer' at layer index 1 (the second decoder layer), selects the top-r% HKVD tokens there, and reuses that same HKVD index set for all subsequent layers. The default recompute ratio r is 0.15-0.18 (15-18%) depending on dataset. See vllm_blend/vllm/model_executor/models/llama.py line 300: cache_fuse_metadata = {'check_layers':[1], 'check': False, 'recomp_ratios':[0.16], 'recomp_ratio':0.16, ...}. For reproduction use a single check layer at index 1 with r in {0.15, 0.16, 0.18}.

resolutions.original_unknown: Which layers run with check_flag=True versus check_flag=False (Section 6 introduces both modes but does not pin the per-layer schedule).
resolutions.resolution: Exactly one layer is 'check': layer index 1 (i.e., the 2nd transformer block). All other layers run with check_flag=False and reuse the HKVD index set selected by layer 1. The model code uses status in {0,1,2}: 0=full prefill, 1=check layer (compute KV diff, pick top-r% HKVD indices), 2=after check (recompute only on those imp_indices).

resolutions.original_unknown: Exact reduction used to compute per-token KV deviation |KV_i[j] - KV_full_i[j]| across heads / channels (L1, L2, max not specified).
resolutions.resolution: L2-squared, summed across both the head dimension and the head_dim (channel) dimension, per token. Code: temp_diff = torch.sum((value[:-last_len,:,:] - value_old[:-last_len,:,:])**2, dim=[1,2]); top_indices = torch.topk(temp_diff, k=topk_num).indices. Equivalent to per-token squared L2 norm of (V_new - V_pre).

resolutions.resolution: Deviation is computed on V (value vectors) only, not on K and not on [K;V]. The implementation only diffs `value` vs `value_old` to select HKVD tokens.

resolutions.original_unknown: Concrete implementation of positional encoding recovery for non-prefix chunks: explicit RoPE re-rotation vs PromptCache-style dummy-prefix precompute (Appendix A only proves invariance).
resolutions.resolution: Explicit RoPE re-rotation. The pre-computed K (stored before RoPE was applied at the original position) is re-rotated by calling the same rotary_emb operator with the NEW absolute positions of the concatenated context (cache_fuse_metadata['org_pos']). A 'fake_q' of the same shape as q is passed to satisfy the kernel signature, then discarded. Concretely: _, old_kv[0] = self.rotary_emb(cache_fuse_metadata['org_pos'], cache_fuse_metadata['fake_q'], old_kv[0]). This implies pre-computed K is stored UN-ROTATED (or its rotation is undone by the convention of always re-applying at new positions).

resolutions.original_unknown: Exact hash function for chunks (paper defers to 'same as vLLM block hashing').
resolutions.resolution: vLLM's prefix-block hash. The mature LMCache implementation calls vllm.utils.hashing.get_hash_fn_by_name('sha256_cbor') (or older alias sha256_cbor_64bit), which is SHA-256 over a CBOR-serialized tuple of (parent_hash, token_id_block); for older vLLM versions builtin Python hash() is the fallback. For a fresh reproduction use sha256_cbor over the chunk's token id list.

resolutions.original_unknown: Exact dtype / quantization of stored KV caches on disk; PerTokenKVSize formula is referenced abstractly.
resolutions.resolution: KV cache is stored in the model's native activation dtype (typically fp16 for Mistral-7B / Llama, bf16 also supported). The CacheBlend prototype records `cache_fuse_metadata['kv_cache_dtype'] = value.dtype` from the live tensor; no quantization is applied to stored KV. Standard formula: PerTokenKVSize(LLM) = 2 (K and V) * num_layers * num_kv_heads * head_dim * dtype_bytes. For Mistral-7B fp16: 2*32*8*128*2 = 131,072 bytes/token (128 KiB).

resolutions.original_unknown: Exact synchronization primitive used by synchronize() (CUDA event vs threading.Event).

The conceptual implementation would use a torch.cuda.Stream + torch.cuda.Event for the GPU loading thread and threading.Thread + threading.Event on the host side. resolutions.original_unknown: Exact normalization / scaling used inside attention when Q is restricted to selected tokens (paper says 'same attention module' but does not specify whether softmax denominator uses all tokens, which is standard).
resolutions.resolution: Standard softmax denominator over ALL keys (selected query attends to every key/value in the layer's full sequence). The code expands K and V back to the full sequence after writing the recomputed entries (`key_old[imp_indices] = key; value_old[imp_indices] = value; key = key_old; value = value_old`) before calling xformers memory_efficient_attention with a LowerTriangularFromBottomRightMask. So softmax is taken over the full key axis with the standard 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling.

resolutions.original_unknown: Whether mask expansion uses the loaded K_pre directly or applies positional recovery on-the-fly per layer.
resolutions.resolution: Positional recovery is applied per-layer on the fly. At each transformer block when status in {1,2}, rotary_emb is re-applied to the loaded K with the new absolute positions BEFORE the K is used to construct the full-length key tensor for attention. This means the stored K_pre is rotation-free / dummy-position and recovered each layer.

resolutions.original_unknown: Behavior when fetch_kv returns -1 mid-pipeline (paper says falls back to recompute, but exact branch not specified).
resolutions.resolution: Implemented conceptually as: if fetch_kv returns -1 for any chunk, set check_flag=False for the request and run a normal full prefill on that chunk's tokens (status=0 path in xformers.py). For partial misses, the missing chunk's tokens become indices that are always included in HKVD (full recompute). The released code path for this is implicit: it simply does the full prefill (status=0) when cache_fuse_metadata['check'] is False.

resolutions.original_unknown: Exact PerTokenKVSize formula and dtype assumed.
resolutions.resolution: Duplicate of dtype unknown above. Concrete formula: PerTokenKVSize(LLM) = 2 (K + V) * num_hidden_layers * num_key_value_heads * head_dim * sizeof(activation_dtype). For Llama-70B (80 layers, 8 kv-heads, head_dim 128) fp16: 2 * 80 * 8 * 128 * 2 = 327,680 B/token.
